title: Microbatch Accordion Binner with Kernel Hinting and Prefill-aware Trimming
creator: Ananya Rao
description: Goal: Reduce padding waste and CPU/GPU kernel mismatch penalties for diverse sequence-length workloads by introducing an 'accordion' bucketing strategy that dynamically resizes buckets at runtime and surfaces kernel-hint metadata to the scheduler. Background: Current static bucketing and length-based coalescers still suffer in high-variance traffic (chatty short messages mixed with long contexts) — we pay token and kernel inefficiency (suboptimal kernel selection, poor occupancy) when many microbatches pad to long seqlen. Approach: 1) Accordion Buckets: buckets are parameterized by a compressibility factor; short-heavy tails cause nearby buckets to collapse (narrow width) while long-tail regions expand, creating an accordion-like histogram that adapts every N seconds. 2) Kernel Hint Score: each incoming request computes a lightweight kernel hint (int8 score) indicating preferred kernel path (e.g., fused attention, flash attention, sparse-aware) based on seqlen and sparse-attn probability. The scheduler uses hints to place microbatches on GPU lanes with matching kernel availability. 3) Prefill-aware Trimming: during prefill, detect repeat-prefix-heavy requests and opportunistically trim cached prefixes to reduce prefill length; the runtime tags prefill operations with TTL and recency to avoid cache poisoning. 4) Graceful latency control: for latency-sensitive routes, the accordion binner biases to smaller buckets with faster kernel choices and accepts some throughput loss; for cost-oriented routes, it prioritizes pad reduction and higher occupancy. Metrics and targets: - 15–25% token-padding reduction on mixed traffic traces (measured by pad_delta) - 7–12% per-token GPU time reduction for Web-chat customers - Maintain P95 latency within current SLO for latency-priority routes Implementation plan: - Phase A (PoC): simulate accordion bucketing offline on 30 days of prod traces, implement kernel-hint encoder in runtime (C++/Rust hot-path). (Owner: Marcus) - Phase B (Canary): integrate into prefill pipeline with canary on a small percentage of traffic, add metrics (pad_ratio, kernel-mismatch-rate, slot-occupancy). (Owner: Marcus + Runtime team) - Phase C (Rollout): policy knobs in Console (bucket aggressiveness, kernel-hint weight, prefill-trim threshold), docs and SDK hints. Risks & trade-offs: - Kernel hint noise can misroute and cause more cold kernel invocations; mitigate with smoothing window and fallback. - Prefill trimming risks correctness for apps relying on exact prefix semantics; default off for routes with strict determinism. - Complexity increases scheduler decision space; add guard rails and A/B evaluation. Success criteria: measurable pad reduction with neutral or improved latency for P1 routes; dashboarded regression alerts for any increase in tail latency or error rates.
